text.p: Hindalco Ltd, India's largest private aluminium company, is currently raising its 210,000 tonnes per year capacity by 32,000 tonnes and is studying proposals to build a 250,000 tonnes per year greenfield smelter, a company official said on Tuesday.
Hindalco sales director Vijay Mushran told a Metal Bulletin conference that India's aluminium industry was expanding production amid hopes of growing demand.
Low-cost natural resources supported this process.
India's nominal annual aluminium capacity today was 670,000 tonnes and a further 75,000 tonnes was idle because of a lack of access to cheap power.
Actual production at 530,000 tonnes per year compared with domestic demand at 580,000, but the major foreign supplier, Russia, might be unable to keep up the current level of exports in the future.
India had vast bauxite reserves of 2.9 billion tonnes and bauxite production prices of $16 per tonne compared with $30 in the western world.
Rolled product capacity stood at 240,000 tonnes per year but plans were in hand to raise this to 470,000 by the year 2000.
Annual foil capacity of 30,000 tonnes should be doubled by the year 2001, as Hindalco planned a new plant to serve such emerging markets as food packaging, cable wrap and pharmaceutical foils.
India's extrusion capacity was put at 150,000 tonnes per year.
Mushran said demand for castings from the automotive sector should grow by 20 percent each year as a number of international carmakers had started operations in India.
The drinks can industry was also just emerging. Presently, India only had filling lines for imported cans.
